summary: The note surveys how schools have prioritized student mental health since September 2023, describing programs from preschool through high school. Examples include counselor-led programs, student clubs, curriculum integration, teacher training, partnerships with mental health professionals, parent seminars, anti-stigma campaigns, and virtual support. It concludes that these efforts have brought reduced absenteeism, better academic performance, and less bullying.
one_line: Overview of school mental health initiatives from 2023-2024, spanning counseling programs, student clubs, teacher training, parent seminars, partnerships, and virtual support.
key_facts: Harper's Elementary School launched "Mind Matters" on October 10, 2023, led by guidance counselor Mrs. Deborah Lane; it includes weekly mindfulness sessions, peer support networks, and resources for parents and teachers.

Lincoln High School students founded the "Green Ribbon Club" as of November 15, 2023, working with school counselors and local mental health professionals to host workshops that destigmatize asking for help.

Rosewood Middle School educators began infusing lesson plans with resilience, empathy, and self-awareness elements by December 1, 2023; Assistant Principal Julia Mendez supports this integrated approach.

New Beginnings Preschool has run its "Happy Hearts" program since September 2023, with daily activities helping preschoolers identify and articulate feelings; director Emma Clarkson says children as young as three are learning to use their words.
City Academy held a professional development day on February 15, 2024, focused entirely on mental health training, including recognizing signs of anxiety and depression.
Johnson Secondary School announced a collaboration with the Community Health Center on January 7, 2024, giving students regular access to therapists and mental health workshops.
Oakwood School District launched monthly parenting seminars on February 22, 2024, on recognizing mental health issues and fostering communication at home.
Meadowvale Middle School's "Mental Health Matters" week started March 14, 2024, with activities and talks to break down stigma.
Riverside High School introduced the Virtual Well-Being Hub on April 12, 2024, so students can access mental health resources regardless of location or circumstances.
Marcus Thompson, a 17-year-old Lincoln High School student, said the Green Ribbon Club taught him that "it's okay to not be okay sometimes."
Mrs. Lane says the focus is now on early intervention and giving children a space to express emotions.
The note cites reduced absenteeism, improved academic performance, lower instances of bullying, and enhanced school culture as observed impacts.
